headline: GENESIS SWALLOWS VAULT MINERALS — Australian Gold Merger Legally Effective Today; Deal Implements November 26, Reshaping WA Gold Sector
snippet: Genesis Minerals' (ASX: GMD) scheme to acquire Vault Minerals became legally effective November 17 after receiving Federal Court of Western Australia approval, backed by 99.74% of Vault shareholders. The deal implements November 26, combining two of WA's leading gold producers and positioning Genesis as one of Australia's largest gold companies by market cap — a significant consolidation in a sector under price pressure.

headline: SILVER BLEEDS MORE THAN GOLD IN SELL-OFFS — FXStreet: $3,500 Gold Possible as Miner Leverage Flips Negative
snippet: FXStreet analysis published November 17 argues that silver and junior mining stocks decline harder than gold itself when equity markets sell off — the same leverage that amplifies gains in bull markets is now amplifying losses as macro headwinds dominate. The author targets gold at approximately $3,500 as the next major support level, warning retail investors long miners and silver as inflation hedges that the correlation structure has inverted in the current risk-off environment.

headline: NEW OWNER PLOTS RESTART AT SHUTTERED PATAGONIA MINE — Nov 16 Filing Revives Stalled South American Gold-Silver Asset
snippet: A November 16 GlobeNewswire release details a new ownership structure and phased restart plan for a previously shuttered gold and silver mine in Patagonia, South America, with fresh capital committed to returning the asset to production. The deal illustrates continued strategic interest in Patagonian precious metals despite the broader sector selloff, and represents the kind of asset-level opportunism that tends to emerge during prolonged bear markets.

headline: URNM ETF AT YEAR LOW $37.76 — Miners Down 31% as Spot Uranium Up 10%; Cost Inflation Crushes Leverage Thesis
snippet: The Sprott Uranium Miners ETF (URNM) fell to a year low of $37.76 on November 16 — its lowest close since May 2025 — even as spot uranium traded around $90.25/lb, up roughly 10% year to date. A November 2026 analysis argues the widening divergence reflects cost inflation compressing miner margins and negative AI-related market sentiment, rather than any fundamental change to the uranium demand thesis; the long-term contract price hit a record $98/lb in October.

headline: LI-FT DRILLS 45m AT 2.71% LiO AT ADINA — Quebec Hard Rock Lithium Advances to PEA Stage With Strong Infill Grades
snippet: Li-FT Power (TSX-V: LIFT) reported a high-grade interval of 45 metres at 2.71% lithium oxide at its Adina project in Quebec, with the intersection extending the established mineralization corridor ahead of a planned preliminary economic assessment. The result arrives amid a broadly bearish lithium market — Chinese battery-grade lithium carbonate is down roughly 14.7% over the past 30 days — but reinforces the project's grade profile as a low-cost brine producers dominate the current pricing environment.

headline: ABEN GOLD DRILLS 7.6m AT 3.66 g/t AU AT JUSTIN, YUKON — First 2026 Assays Hit; Four More Holes Still Pending
snippet: Aben Gold (TSX-V: ABM) reported its first 2026 assay results from the Justin project in Yukon's Toodoggone District, with the opening hole returning 7.6 metres at 3.66 g/t gold from the POW Zone — a solid opening result for the program. Four additional holes from the 2026 campaign are awaiting assays, with the company targeting a resource update later in the year; the Justin project sits in the same prolific Toodoggone corridor as several other junior gold explorers.

headline: PANTHER MINERALS ENTERS NEW MEXICO URANIUM — Acquires Mesa Top Property in State With Revived Nuclear Ambitions
snippet: Panther Minerals (TSX-V) is acquiring the Mesa Top uranium property in New Mexico, subject to exchange acceptance, marking the company's entry into a US state with growing strategic importance for domestic uranium supply. The deal reflects a broader trend of junior uranium companies expanding their US-jurisdiction footprint ahead of anticipated growth in nuclear power demand, even as URNM equity prices hit year lows.

headline: COPPER, LITHIUM, GOLD, SILVER ALL DOWN IN 30-DAY SWEEP — CW46 Roundup Shows No Mining Sector Left Untouched by Dollar Surge
snippet: The Mining SEE weekly roundup for calendar week 46 (November 10–16) confirms a broad commodity retreat across all major sectors tracked by retail mining investors: LME copper fell approximately 7% over 30 days to a four-month low near $13,211/t, Chinese battery-grade lithium carbonate dropped roughly 14.7%, gold slid toward a 14-month low near $3,832, and silver gave back 34.75% year to date. The uniform cross-commodity selloff reflects dollar strength, rising US rate expectations, and sluggish Chinese economic data rather than any single sector-specific catalyst.

headline: FIVE DISCIPLINED CANADIAN MINERS TO WATCH — TSX Names That Have Held Ground Through the 2026 Selloff
snippet: Canadian Mining Report identifies five TSX-listed gold miners maintaining balance sheet discipline and demonstrating operational resilience during the 2026 selloff, with the analysis focusing on companies that generate free cash flow at current gold prices rather than requiring a recovery to break even. The piece offers a framework for distinguishing value from value traps in the current environment — directly relevant for self-directed investors trying to build a watchlist in a prolonged bear market.

headline: NEWMONT'S $1,520 AISC THE BULL CASE AT $3,850 GOLD — Investing.com Names 10 Miners That Could Lead the Rebound
snippet: Investing.com profiles 10 mining stocks it considers most likely to lead a recovery, noting Newmont (NYSE: NEM) has lowered its 2026 all-in sustaining cost target to approximately $1,520 per ounce — a margin of roughly $2,300 at current spot prices — as the benchmark for a sustainable recovery thesis. Goldman Sachs maintains a year-end gold price target of $4,900 per ounce, implying a potential 27% recovery from current levels of $3,850, though the consensus view calls for further headwinds ahead of the December FOMC decision.
